To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CD25(?) Treg cells isolated in vitro from HIV-infected subjects suppress the cytolytically and nonlytically antiviral activity (e.g., chemokine production and cytokine expression) of HIV-specific CTL in vitro.
CD25( + ) Tregs isolated from HIV-inflicted patients suppress the antiviral function of HIV-specific CD4(+) and CD8( +) T cells, which may contribute to the impaired immune response to HIV in vivo.
CD25(?) Tregs suppress cytolytic function of HIV-specific T cell in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of regulatory T cells in modulating HIV-specific T cell function.
the immunopathogenesis of HIV disease
the role of CD25(?) regulatory T cells in the control of HIV replication and the impact of these cells on HIV-specific CD8 T cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD25+ T regulatory cells are a significant factor in the suppression of HIV-specific cytolytic T cell activity and the ability of HIV-specific CD 8 T cells to secrete HIV-inhibitory cytokines.

HIV infection is characterized not only by a progressive decline in the number of CD4(+) and CD8(+) lymphocytes, but also by a loss of the ability of CD8(+) cells to lyse virus infected cells and to produce cytokines and chemokines that inhibit viral replication.
CD25(?)Treg cells isolated from HIV infected individuals can inhibit cytolytic and cytokine production by HIV specific CD8+ T cell responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV infection is characterized, in part, by an increase in CD25(+) regulatory T cells.
HIV-specific T cell function can be suppressed in vitro by CD25(+) regulatory T cells.
CD25(?)Tregs are immunosuppressive and can suppress the cytolyic activity of HIV specific CTLs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV infection is characterized in part by a loss of CD25( +) regulatory T cells, which are a subset of CD4(+) helper T cells that are immunosuppressive.
